correctness.rationale: Every code has common endpoint orientation; after reversal its word supports are (i,j,n). A two-direction proof shows non-overlap iff min(i)+min(j)>n. This bounds every code by a fully feasible threshold family of size (a-1)(2n-3a)/2; integer optimization proves all three formulas and equality rigidity. Finite exhaustive tests of all oriented subsets n=4..9, literal overlap criteria n=4..21, and constructions n=4..30 corroborate the proof; they are not used as infinite proof.

evidence: General unconstrained upper/lower bounds and constructions need not be attained by the subfamily of weight-three words.
Variable-length non-overlapping size bounds compare to unrestricted fixed-length maxima, not a classification of a prescribed-weight layer.
broader_coverage.reasoning: To imply this result a general code theorem must determine both the exact capacity under weight three at every length and equality cases. The inspected broader bounds and construction statements do not provide those conclusions; the new explicit minimizer criterion is needed.

evidence: The new theorem gives a necessary-and-sufficient inequality in two ordered support coordinates; that structural conclusion is not supplied by the inspected general constructions.
The equality case identifies precisely two or four labeled maxima, which is strictly more information than existence or unrestricted size estimates.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A generic non-overlapping code construction may attain an unrestricted optimum without reaching the prescribed weight-three capacity or describing all equality cases. The prior claims are compared by logical implication rather than title similarity; none inspected implies the present complete weight-three rigidity theorem.

evidence: The generating-function paper studies general non-overlapping code constructions and enumerators, not a classification of all fixed-weight-three optimal codebooks.
The non-expandability paper characterizes enlargement properties of specific code families rather than the complete weight-three optimal slice.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Non-overlap and cross-bifix-freeness are equivalent naming conventions; this equivalence was taken into account. In the inspected material, neither name was accompanied by the exact all-n fixed-weight-three formula and rigidity statement. Search absence alone is not a proof of novelty.

evidence: The unrestricted binary length-five optimum is two; its agreement with the proposed weight-three value at that single length does not cover the all-length capacity and exact labeled classification.
No checked exact table or database statement was found encompassing all three residue classes and complete equality cases.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The exact parameter constraint is Hamming weight three, with all codewords same length and self-overlaps included. Neither matching isolated unrestricted numbers nor generic tables establish the new general theorem; an unindexed fixed-content table remains possible.

originality.rationale: The four inspected primary works concern broader unrestricted or variable-length sizes and non-expandability, but the exact all-n prescribed-weight-three capacity and complete optimal-code classification are not implied by the inspected statements. The key two-interior-one criterion supplies a novel direct reduction; unindexed equivalents remain possible.
residual_risks: A differently named constant-composition synchronization result may state the same exact formula or threshold-classification in material not located during the checks.
A much stronger unexamined general non-overlap characterization could logically subsume the theorem.

evidence: General q-ary constructions and generating-function framework; no assertion of exact all-length weight-three optimum or classification in inspected sections.
